body.statement: With \(t=t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}\) in \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\), does a conditional-modulus interval whose realized radius is \(\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha)\) attain the sharp asymptotic minimax constant for \(L_n^\star/r_n\) uniformly over all finite or infinite limits of \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\), while retaining \(P\in\mathcal M\), bounded \(Y\), and the measurable envelope \(c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa\)?  Equivalently, can one prove that the candidate interval is uniformly honest despite the convention \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha)=0\) when the affine feasible set is empty, and that \(2\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)\)---the candidate untruncated expected full length---matches the minimax expected full interval length and a least-favorable mixed regular-plus-local experiment in the regular, critical, atom-dominated, and fixed-threshold regimes?  This question does not assert that the zero-totalized candidate is honest, nondegenerate, or optimal.
body.justification: The explicit realized-design modulus is only a candidate radius; deciding its coverage and exact constant would complete the order-optimal expected-length theory.
body.gap: Fixed-design convex-modulus theory does not settle the moving random design, the mixed regular-plus-local experiment, or the zero-totalized singular-design behavior under a merely measurable polynomial density envelope.
body.consumer: A positive resolution would determine the shortest defensible full-length interval and its calibrated multiplier for the official threshold-policy workflow; a negative resolution would rule out this zero-totalized candidate.
